summary: I reproduced the gap on the local source (5e2992b, read-only, untouched). The benchmark's minimal replay gives outer 4.82 s, internal 2.47 s and a gap of 2.37 s with load_all (median of 3). On a byte-compiled local install the gap is 1.76 s. Removing only the dead `if (!exists("x")) x = NULL` branch cuts the traced gap from 1.53 s to 0.055 s. On a T03-like workspace I replayed the recorded request-2 code through mcp_dispatch_local at N=1231 tables. Median outer was 10.36 s, internal 1.37 s and the gap 8.99 s. Of that, pre-gate was 4.42 s and the gate 4.44 s. About 97% of the gap (8.73 s) is env_snap_size(raw), called from the risk classifier's note_assign for the dead `raw = list(...)` assignment. The classifier runs twice per call: once in mcp_serve_exec and again in perm_decide -> call_risk. Each run costs about 4.4 s. Inside env_snap_size the time goes to string deduplication: per-vector unique.default plus two unique(unlist()) passes over about 86M stored string pointers. It walks 715 of the 1231 tables before sampling. unique.default is 64% of profiled self time and unlist 12%. The sizing also allocates about 4.5 GB on top of the 6.0 GB workspace. The gap grows with N (0.48 / 1.00 / 2.91 / 8.99 s at N=25/100/300/1231) and with character columns: numeric-only tables at N=1231 give a 0.50 s gap. Code without the fallback (b) stays at 0.18-0.20 s for every N; read-only code (c) is 0.065 s and assigning a new name (d) 0.085 s. Modifying raw (e) costs 10.6 s of gap, plus 5.0 s inside checkpoint_after and 5.2 s after the tool in env_on_agent_end, all re-sizing raw. The native agent-loop route pays the same: two classifications, gap 7.97 s at N=1231, 95% env_snap_size. I tried three throwaway experimental fixes on copies of the source, at N=1231 (request-2/request-3 gaps). Reusing the first risk result in the gate: 3.55 s. Caching the size by address plus fingerprint: 0.25/0.40 s. Skipping the size entirely, as a lower bound: 0.24/0.33 s. The local per-phase times are about 2.9x faster than the AWS ones (4.4 vs 12.8-13.4 s); this is inference, not measured on AWS.

causes.title: A dead assignment in the code makes the static risk classifier compute the full size of the multi-GB object it would overwrite
causes.where: R/perm-classify.R:3090-3101 (note_assign -> risk_binding_safe), R/perm-classify.R:2277-2300 (risk_binding_info -> risk_binding_leaf -> env_snap_size), R/utils-size.R:18-44 (env_snap_size)
causes.mechanism: For every top-level assignment, note_assign looks up the existing binding. If one exists, it calls env_snap_size() on it to write 'overwrites `raw` <list, 4.5 GB>' and to raise the level from 2 to 3 above gptr.protect_size (1e8; R/perm-classify.R:2610 and :3100). The branch never runs, because raw exists, but the static walk still sees `raw = list(...)`, so the full size walk runs on the 1231-table list. Reading raw (variant c) or assigning a new name (variant d) never reaches env_snap_size.
causes.cost: Measured, N=1231 tables, recorded request-2 code, MCP route, median of 3: env_snap_size via risk_binding_leaf took 8.73 s of the 8.99 s gap (97%). For request-3 code it was 9.10 of 9.46 s (96%). With the fallback block removed (variant b) the gap is 0.195 s (b2) / 0.416 s (b3) at every N. Minimal replay on the byte-compiled install: sizing x twice inside the classifier took about 1.06 s of the 1.53 s gap (70%).
causes.safety_role: Shows the person the size of what would be overwritten and raises the level to 3 when it exceeds protect_size. The protect_size policy (R/perm-gate.R:200-206) asks only in default/edits mode and returns NULL in auto/yolo. Auto mode allows any non-control level below 4 (R/perm-gate.R:127), so in the benchmark's auto mode the exact byte count did not change the decision (source reading). A bounded or cached size would keep the level-3 threshold.
causes.scales_with: Number of tables walked (linear up to the sampling cut at about 715 tables, then two dedupe passes) times the number of character columns. Numeric-only tables cost 0.11 s per sizing at N=1231 against about 4.4 s with 3 character columns. Also once per overwritten existing name (request 3 has 16 names; only raw is expensive).

causes.title: Risk is classified twice per tool call, in both the MCP route and the native route
causes.where: MCP: R/mcp-server.R:269-273 (risk.classify before the gate) and R/mcp-server.R:281 -> :192 perm_check -> R/agent-dispatch.R:587-590 perm_decide -> call_risk R/agent-dispatch.R:852-875 (:869). Native: R/agent-dispatch.R:96 (call_risk as tool_call_hook's risk argument) and :99 -> :590.
causes.mechanism: perm_decide always recomputes the risk 'from the raw input' (R/agent-dispatch.R:572-573) and never uses the classification the caller just made, so the whole classification, including C1's size walk, runs again inside the gate. In the native route the first call_risk is a lazy argument of tool_call_hook, so its time shows up under tool_call_hook.
causes.cost: Measured, N=1231, request-2 code, MCP route: classification 1 (pre-gate) 4.41 s (49.1% of gap), classification 2 (in the gate) 4.42 s (49.2%). Native N=1231: 3.74 + 3.88 s. Experimental copy that reuses the first risk when the input is identical: gap 8.99 -> 3.55 s (request 2) and 9.46 -> 3.55 s (request 3), median of 3.
causes.safety_role: The second classification sees the input as it actually runs, in case a tool_call hook rewrote it (decision 'modify'; R/agent-dispatch.R:126-127). A policy 'modify' is reclassified separately (R/agent-dispatch.R:595-599) and is unaffected. An identical() check on the input keeps that guarantee (the experiment in src/x-reuse did this).
causes.scales_with: Whatever one classification costs (C1 and C3); it doubles them.

causes.title: env_snap_size's string deduplication dominates the size walk
causes.where: R/utils-size.R:133-136 (unique.default of every character vector into st$strs), R/utils-size.R:66-69 (env_size_strings: unique(unlist(mget()))), called at R/utils-size.R:209 (sampled-list extrapolation) and R/utils-size.R:42 (final count); budget R/utils-size.R:48
causes.mechanism: To count each distinct CHARSXP once, the walk deduplicates each character column (3 per table, 60,664 strings each). It then deduplicates the union of all stored vectors twice: once when the 1231-item list is sampled, and once at the end. The parts budget (10,000) cuts the walk after 715 tables, so about 715 x 120k = 86M string pointers are deduplicated twice. Every table's columns are separate STRSXPs, so the address cache never skips them.
causes.cost: Measured in size-parts.R, N=1231, median of 3: env_snap_size(raw) 3.72 s, of which the two dedupe passes take 2.28 s (61%) and the walk, including per-vector unique.default, 1.48 s (39%). At N=300: 1.11 s (one pass, 0.49 s). Elapsed-event Rprof of the whole request-2 call (rep 2): unique.default 63.8% self, unlist 12.2%, GC 5.2%. Memory, measured in size-direct: gc max used 10,546 MB against 6,013 MB live raw at N=1231, about 4.5 GB transient per sizing.
causes.safety_role: An honest object size for shared strings, following the package's one size rule (R/utils-size.R:1-17), also used for workspace descriptions and checkpoint budgets. What is lost by replacing it is accuracy of the reported bytes, not a permission decision in auto mode.
causes.scales_with: min(N, about 715) tables x character columns x strings per column, plus the second dedupe pass once a list has more than about 715 items. Numeric columns are O(1) per vector.

causes.title: Checkpoint snapshots re-size a big binding when it is first seen or has changed
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:464 (ckpt_objects_before) and :547 (ckpt_objects_after) -> env_snapshot -> R/env-snapshot.R:163-170 (sizes reused only when address/class/shape/fp match). Pure reads skip the checkpoint (R/ckpt-rewind.R:37-41, :58).
causes.mechanism: The objects checkpointer snapshots the workspace before and after each non-read call. An unchanged raw reuses the previous bytes (requests 2 and 3: about 0.1 s). A first-seen or modified raw is re-sized with env_snap_size: in checkpoint_before when the checkpointer has no earlier snapshot of raw, and in checkpoint_after when raw was created or changed.
causes.cost: Measured at N=1231. First non-read call after raw exists (rep 1 of each run): checkpoint_before 3.7-4.7 s. Variant e (raw$x = 1): checkpoint_after 5.04 s (internal 5.11 s; 3.4 s in the no-size run). Requests 2 and 3 (raw unchanged): checkpoint_before 0.12 / 0.13 s (1.3% of gap). This is the local analog of T03 request 1's 13.9 s checkpoint_after on AWS (inference). Minimal replay: the first checkpoint_before sizes x, 0.43 s of the 1.53 s gap.
causes.safety_role: Undo/rewind bookkeeping: sizes decide ref/copy/disk/skip against gptr.undo_* budgets (R/ckpt-objects.R:411-420).
causes.scales_with: Size walk of each new or changed binding (C3); nothing when objects are unchanged.

causes.title: The agent_end workspace snapshot re-sizes a changed big object after the tool (harness time outside the tool interval)
causes.where: R/env-snapshot.R:485-490 (env_on_agent_end -> env_view_snapshot -> env_snap_rows), registered at R/env-snapshot.R:530
causes.mechanism: The workspace-changes memory keeps its own snapshot, separate from the checkpointer's ck$snap. When raw changed, this snapshot sizes it again right after the tool call, even though checkpoint_after has just sized it.
causes.cost: Measured, variant e: 5.18 s at N=1231 (request wall minus outer interval 5.40 s) and 1.12 s at N=300. For unchanged raw (requests 2 and 3) wall minus outer is about 0.12 s. Its contribution to A1's extra harness time after request 1 in the original run is inferred, not measured.
causes.safety_role: Lets the next request's <workspace_changes> show only the user's own changes.

causes.title: Fixed per-call gate and checkpoint overhead that does not depend on the workspace
causes.where: R/mcp-server.R:235-307; R/ckpt-objects.R:467 and R/ckpt-files.R:397 (ckpt_predict -> code_targets re-walks the code twice with envir = NULL); R/agent-dispatch.R:635-667 (perm_policies, 6 ext_policy_decide calls); R/perm-gate.R:104-109 (eval_guard)
causes.mechanism: Two classifications of the rest of the code, two extra code walks for checkpoint target prediction, the policy chain, fingerprints of bindings (12-54 calls) and the checkpoint snapshots.
causes.cost: Measured gap medians, constant in N: b2 0.18-0.195 s, b3 0.37-0.42 s (request 3 still overwrites `reference_gene_ids` and others), c 0.061-0.067 s, d 0.077-0.087 s. For b2 at N=1231: checkpoint_before 0.083 s, classifications 0.033 + 0.040 s, ckpt_predict 0.044 s, perm_policies 0.018 s, fingerprint 0.045 s.
causes.safety_role: The gate itself, undo prediction and the policies.
causes.scales_with: Code length and number of assigned names; nearly nothing from object size.

causes.title: Measurement artifact: first-call byte compilation under pkgload::load_all
causes.where: pkgload::load_all loads uncompiled closures; R's JIT compiles them on first use
causes.mechanism: In a fresh process the first classification and policy calls pay JIT compilation (Rprof of the step-1 classification: cmpfun 98% of the first calls; five later calls took 0.009 s). The benchmark's installed package is byte-compiled.
causes.cost: Measured, minimal replay: gap 2.37 s with load_all against 1.76 s on a byte-compiled local install. No-fallback code: 0.63 s against 0.055 s. gate-run.R used two warm-up calls, so the variant timings exclude this.
causes.safety_role: None (an artifact of how the source was loaded).

Each table is its own data.table::fread() of one synthetic GDC STAR Counts TSV: 4 N_* rows plus 60,660 genes; gene_id 'ENSG%011d.%d', about 59,400 distinct gene_name, 40 gene_type; 3 integer and 3 double columns. Every table therefore has fresh STRSXPs whose CHARSXPs are shared through R's global string cache, as real fread output of identical annotation columns has. Live memory 4.9 MB per table. Load average was 8-18 on 16 cores during the runs (single-threaded R). The same quantity varied by about 20-30% between runs, e.g. env_snap_size(raw) at N=1231 took 3.3-5.5 s. Peak RSS went over the ~12 GB guideline twice: 13.8 GB in the N=1231 trace run (guard killed it at e rep 3, after the data was written) and 13.9 GB in the no-size e run.

open_questions: Local per-phase times are about 2.9x faster than AWS (4.4 s vs 12.8-13.4 s per phase). The author's minimal replays show AWS/macOS at 2.2x. The extra factor is unmeasured: it could be AWS memory bandwidth on 86M-pointer hashing, or differences between real and synthetic gene_name/gene_type distinct counts.

AWS checkpoint_before was 1.4/0.8 s in requests 2/3 against 0.12 s here. My project folder had no 1231 input TSVs (5 GB), so a file-checkpointer cost (ckpt_files_before / ckpt_call_paths) on the real project tree is not reproduced.

Whether the exact byte count is needed at all: source reading says auto/yolo ignore protect_size and allow level 3. Default/edits mode needs only 'bytes > gptr.protect_size', so a walk that stops at the threshold should keep decisions identical. This is not tested.

The x-memo fingerprint covers raw's top-level structure, so a data.table edited in place by := keeps the same address and fingerprint and the cached size goes stale. That was acceptable for the experiment; it is not a vetted design.

Request-1 behavior was not replayed with the real fread loop. Its 13.9 s checkpoint_after and a probable second sizing in env_on_agent_end (C5) are inferred from the variant-e mechanism. They may explain part of A1's extra harness time, which is not measured.
Rprof's elapsed sampling covered about 82% of the outer interval (7.12 of 8.68 s), so its percentages are shares of the sampled time only.
